From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jul 1, 2025 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: Burst pools ops readiness (beta): monitoring, paging, disable procedures + oncall coverage

Hi all — per Neha’s ask on last week’s beta gate, here’s the ops readiness checklist for burst pools. Goal is to get explicit sign-off that we have: (1) monitoring + paging, (2) a fast/low-risk disable path, and (3) oncall coverage for the first two weeks of pilot.

Key items (blocking vs non-blocking):

BLOCKING for pilot enablement:
1) Disable procedures (tenant + region scoped)
- “Kill switch” must exist in control plane + routing enforcement (no soft-only). ETA: this week (ties to ENG-4828 / rollout tooling).
- Clear ownership and permissions for who can flip it in an incident (ties to INT-881).
- Target time-to-disable: < 5 minutes from decision.

2) Paging + dashboards
- Pager on: pool saturation >= 90% for > 10 min OR reject rate >= 5% sustained (pilot tenants only).
- Pager on: neighbor p99 drift > 20% vs baseline for > 15 min correlated with burst admit.
- Dashboard panels must exist per region/pool, plus per-tenant admit/deny breakdown.

3) Capacity guardrails
- Minimum reserved headroom for hosted unaffected: burst pools must be isolated and excluded from hosted commitments (infra already aligned, but need written confirmation).
- Per-region maximum burst utilization cap (global circuit breaker).

NON-BLOCKING (can land during week 1 of pilot):
- Better customer-facing error messaging and deny reason codes (docs follow-up)
- Additional forensics log fields (burst claim propagation already in flight)

Asks:
A) Neha: Can you confirm we have exec approval for paging policy (SRE oncall) for the pilot period, and that pausing the beta is acceptable if we trip the circuit breaker threshold?
B) Irene: Please confirm the topology/isolation statement below (so we can reference in launch comms + internal incident docs).
C) Mina: Please confirm routing fallback semantics when burst denied vs pool saturated (do we return 429/503 vs fallback to baseline/other region). We need this in runbook.
D) Lauren: Please confirm pilot window + which tenants are in scope so we can tune alert filters.

Topology/isolation statement (draft):
- Burst pools are separate node pools labeled burst=true, dedicated=false, and are excluded from baseline dedicated reservations.
- Pilot tenants can only burst into pools in the same region as their dedicated tenant unless explicitly configured otherwise.
- Routing never sends hosted traffic into burst pools.

Attachments:
- Burst_Pools_Ops_Readiness_Checklist_v0.6.pdf
- Burst_Pool_Alerting_Panels_Screenshot.png

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Fleet Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Burst pools ops readiness (beta): monitoring, paging, disable procedures + oncall coverage

Vanessa — this is exactly what I needed.

Re (A): yes, you have approval to page SRE oncall for pilot burst-related alerts as long as:
- alerts are scoped to pilot pools/tenants (no “global” pages unless hosted SLO is at risk), and
- we have a documented “pause beta” gate.

“Pause beta” is acceptable if:
- saturation stays >90% for 10 min and reject rate is rising, OR
- we see neighbor p99 drift >20% linked to burst admissions.

Please make sure the kill switch is not gated by a single human being’s permissions. If INT-881 isn’t resolved by Friday, we need an interim plan (e.g., pre-approved operators list + runbook).

-Neha
Neha Kapoor

Subject: Re: Burst pools ops readiness (beta): monitoring, paging, disable procedures + oncall coverage

Confirmed on topology/isolation with one nuance:

- Burst pools are separate node pools labeled burst=true AND tenancy=shared-burst. They are NOT part of any dedicated reservation accounting.
- They are currently in the same regional cluster fabric as hosted, but:
  - hosted routing is explicitly blocked from these pools (routing policy + admission), and
  - quota enforcement is in control plane + data plane to prevent “leakage.”

I’d recommend we adjust the statement to avoid implying physical separation where it’s actually logical + policy isolation.

Also re region constraint: same-region bursting is the default and will be enforced for pilot unless we explicitly whitelist cross-region for a tenant (I don’t expect we will for beta).

-Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Infrastructure Architecture

Re (C) routing semantics:

Baseline behavior (pilot):
1) Request goes to tenant’s baseline dedicated pool.
2) If baseline is at configured limit (concurrency/TPS) AND tenant is burst-enabled, we attempt burst admission.
3) If burst admission allowed AND burst pool has headroom, route to burst pool in same region.

When burst is denied (policy):
- Return 429 with “burst-denied” reason code header (safe enum), no cross-region fallback.
- Rationale: it’s a tenant-configured guardrail and retry should be backed off.

When burst is saturated (pool):
- Return 503 with “burst-unavailable” reason code header.
- Rationale: this is capacity/supply; customer can retry with jitter OR fall back to their own degraded mode.

We will not auto-fallback to hosted from dedicated.

For runbook: suggest we add “how to differentiate deny vs saturated” plus recommended customer guidance (retry-after, backoff) once the error semantics doc lands.

Mina
Mina Haddad
Smart Routing Lead

Updates / decisions captured:
- Topology statement will be revised to “logical + policy isolation in shared regional fabric” (per Irene).
- Pause beta gate and paging scope approved (per Neha). We’ll keep pages scoped to pilot pools/tenants, and only escalate broader if hosted SLO risk is detected.
- Routing semantics for runbook:
  - 429 = burst denied by policy/limits
  - 503 = burst pool unavailable/saturated

Action items (owners / due):
1) Disable path + permissions
- I’m following up on INT-881. If it doesn’t close by Fri, we’ll do an interim allowlist for oncall operators who can flip tenant+region kill switch (documented in runbook).

2) Oncall coverage confirmation
- Fleet: I’ll staff primary for burst pool provisioning + labeling issues for first two weeks of pilot.
- Need SRE confirmation on who is primary for alert response + mitigation steps. Lauren, can you confirm who the pilot DRI is on the product side for comms during incidents (customer updates)?

3) Dashboard/paging finalization
- I’ll sync with the dashboard owner on adding the per-tenant filters + the neighbor p99 drift panel in the default view (ties to ENG-4827).

I’ll send a revised v0.7 checklist tomorrow morning with these changes.

-Vanessa
